about: Loop Laps: predict, then watch the runner trace the loop one lap per pass. `trace` holds the watched variables at the end of each lap, as Python repr. tests/test_gym_games.py runs every snippet under a tracer and checks the laps, the trace and the answer (`expr` evaluated afterwards, or the lap count when kind is laps).

items.ask: How many laps does the loop run?
items.why: total goes 1, 3, 6, 10. Once it is 10, the test total < 10 is False, so the loop stops after 4 laps.

items.ask: What is n when the loop stops?
items.why: 20 → 6 → 2 → 0. 2 is still > 1, so one more pass floors it to 0. The loop never lands on exactly 1.

items.ask: What is total when the loop ends?
items.why: continue jumps straight back to the test, skipping the rest of lap 3, so 3 is never added: 1 + 2 + 4 + 5 = 12.

items.ask: How many laps does the loop run?
items.why: The body runs with n = 5, 4, 3 and 2. When n reaches 1 the test n > 1 fails: 4 laps, and fact ends at 120.

items.ask: What is count when the loop ends?
items.why: range(2, 8) gives 2 up to 7. The stop, 8, is left out, so there are 8 − 2 = 6 laps.

items.ask: What is s when the loop ends?
items.why: len(word) − 1 is 2, so i only takes 0 and 1. The last letter, at index 2, is never reached.

items.ask: What is best when the loop ends?
items.why: range(1, len(nums) − 1) stops at index 2, so the last number, 9, is never checked. One too few in the bound gives 7.

items.ask: What is squares when the loop ends?
items.why: range(1, 4) gives 1, 2 and 3. The stop, 4, is left out, so 16 never appears.

items.ask: What is picked when the loop ends?
items.why: With and, both parts must hold. 8 is even but not over 9, so only 10 and 12 count.

items.ask: What is pos after the call?
items.why: Lap 1 checks "ana": no match. In lap 2 names[1] is "bo", so return 1 ends the function in the middle of the loop. "cy" is never looked at.

items.ask: After y = bump(), what is the global x?
items.why: x = 1 inside bump makes a new local x. The loop changes that local (1, 2, 4); the global x stays 10.

items.ask: What is total when the loop ends?
items.why: int(p) turns each piece of text into a number, so the loop adds 3 + 4 + 5. Without int() it would raise TypeError.
